title: Airwolf (TV series)
intro: Airwolf is the fictional supersonic armed helicopter of the TV series Airwolf (1984-1987), a modified Bell 222 with guns that fold out of the body, a missile pod and turbo thrusters. Two pilots sit in front, and a flight engineer's weapons and systems station is behind them.

areas.name: Instrument panel
areas.text: Displays and lit switches in front of the pilots.

panels.name: Instrument panel
panels.text: Screens, lit switch rows and the turbo control in front of the pilots.
panels.context: The series shows a busy, glowing panel; the turbo control gives Airwolf its famous speed.

controls.name: Displays
controls.text: Screens show the flight data and the targeting pictures.
controls.context: They help the pilot fly and aim the weapons.

controls.name: Turbo thrusters

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The turbo thrusters push the helicopter to very high speed.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: Airwolf flies like a normal fast helicopter.

controls.text: This control switches on the turbo thrusters, jet engines that push Airwolf to very high speed, faster than sound.
controls.context: No normal helicopter can fly this fast; it is how Airwolf escapes or catches up. The exact control is not identified.

controls.name: Lit switch rows
controls.text: Rows of lit switches for Airwolf's systems.
controls.context: The series shows them glowing in the dark cockpit; each one is not explained.

panels.name: Co-pilot seat
panels.text: The second pilot seat beside the pilot in Airwolf.
panels.context: In the series Dominic Santini often sits here.

controls.name: Co-pilot seat
controls.text: The second pilot seat, where Dominic Santini sits in the series.
controls.context: A second pilot can fly or help with the systems.

areas.name: Weapons and systems console
areas.text: The flight engineer's station behind the pilots.

panels.name: Weapons and systems console
panels.text: The flight engineer's station with the weapon selection and electronics.
panels.context: From here the weapons are armed and the scanners and countermeasures are run.

controls.name: Weapon selection
controls.text: A selector that arms the chain guns or the missiles from this station.
controls.context: The pilot then fires the selected weapon with the trigger on the cyclic.

controls.name: Electronics
controls.text: Scanners and countermeasures, things that fool enemy missiles.
controls.context: The engineer watches for threats and protects the helicopter.

areas.name: Cyclic and collective
areas.text: The hand controls the pilot flies with.

panels.name: Cyclic
panels.text: The cyclic stick in front of the pilot in Airwolf.
panels.context: It tilts the helicopter to fly forward, back and sideways.

controls.name: Cyclic
controls.text: Pushing the cyclic forward tips the helicopter forward so it flies forward; moving it sideways makes it fly sideways.
controls.context: It tilts the rotor in the direction the pilot wants to go.

controls.name: Weapons trigger
controls.text: A trigger on the cyclic grip fires the selected weapon.
controls.context: The weapon is chosen at the flight engineer's station; the guns fold out of the body before firing.

panels.name: Collective
panels.text: The collective lever at the pilot's left hand.
panels.context: It makes the helicopter climb or sink.

controls.name: Collective
controls.text: Pulling the collective up makes the rotor blades bite more air so the helicopter climbs; pushing it down makes it sink.
controls.context: Together with the cyclic it is how every helicopter is flown.
